title: Empty-input rejection by the guard
statement: For every finite Turing machine $M$ over the Boolean alphabet, the nonempty-input guard of $M$, on the empty input, halts after one step and outputs exactly the one-symbol word $[\mathrm{false}]$, using some amount of work-tape space.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
replaced:
For every finite machine $M$, the nonempty-input guard of $M$, run on the empty
input, is halted after one step with output exactly the single bit false.
